questions: Is the modulus for the final answer 998244353, as typical for many competitive programming problems, or should it be read from the input?
Should intermediate calculations (like product of sequence elements) be reduced modulo 998244353 to avoid overflow, or is arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic expected?
When computing f(S_i/S_{i+1}) = P*Q for the reduced fraction P/Q, is the fraction reduced to lowest terms using positive coprime integers, even if S_i and S_i+1 are not coprime?
For the condition gcd(S_1,...,S_N)=1, is the gcd computed over all N elements, and must it hold for the entire sequence, not just pairwise?
Are the S_i required to be positive integers, and is there an upper bound on their values (like 10^9) or can they be arbitrarily large as long as they satisfy the conditions?
Is the score defined as the product of all S_i (i.e., S_1 * S_2 * ... * S_N), and should this product be computed exactly before taking modulo, or can it be computed modulo throughout?
If multiple good sequences exist, should the sum of their scores be computed modulo 998244353, and is the modulo operation applied only at the end or also to each score individually?
Does the condition f(S_i/S_{i+1}) = A_i apply for all i from 1 to N-1, and is the fraction S_i/S_{i+1} considered as a rational number, not necessarily in lowest terms initially?
